rationale: Review discusses turmeric-derived curcumin in experimental formulations, including non-dietary applications, without a culinary pain comparison.
Drug-delivery review discusses orange-derived extracellular vesicles as engineered cancer-targeting carriers, not culinary orange or Parkinson outcomes.
Human olfactory testing uses cinnamon as an odor cue; identification did not distinguish study groups, and ingestion was not tested.
Grape juice is a biosensor validation matrix. The analytical test does not measure a clinical response after consuming grapes.
This review describes ginger-derived particles in a preclinical colitis context. Culinary ginger and the assigned Parkinson outcome are untested.
Depression delivery review describes ginger-derived nanoparticles interacting with gut microbes; no independent culinary ginger treatment outcome is established.
Alzheimer mouse study uses corn oil as vehicle for tamoxifen; this does not isolate a dietary corn-oil outcome.
Review describes salmon-derived DNA in a biomimetic material, not dietary salmon or a Parkinson motor comparison.
Parkinson-model rats receive sunflower oil as injectable vehicle; coordination and exploration were assessed, not oil-only rigidity.
Cell-death review describes curcumin as a turmeric constituent; Agent Orange denotes a herbicide, not orange fruit.
A figure documents undigested millet seeds in a veterinary digestive-impaction case. No culinary human exposure or Parkinson symptom outcome is measured.
The laboratory comparator does not establish a culinary grapeseed exposure, pain effect, or product linkage to NCT07630571.
